chapter_title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant. Paragraphs 2-7 form a complete, self-contained four-fold cosmological teaching about the weeping of the light elements (garments/sons of the First Man) at four stages of the cosmic drama. The enumeration structure (first, second, third, fourth) is systematic and internally complete. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system: cosmic beings weep at cosmic events. The teaching cycle closes naturally at P7 with the explanation of why the fourth weeping is worst. P8 then bridges to apostolic mission with 'Therefore, due to' — a classic editorial seam extending the completed teaching to justify apostolic suffering. P9 is a brief closing exhortation. No editorial bridge or institutional vocabulary intrudes into the core teaching sequence. No NT citations detected. Negative editorial fatigue score (-0.52) is consistent with the editorial material being brief and confined to the end.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic dialogue frame. 'Once again he speaks to his disciples' — no cosmological content, no substantive question. Bridge connective flag fires but this is simply the standard frame formula.

paragraphs.core_text: The garments, the sons of the First Man, wept bitterly three times. Then they were silent. There is a fourth time of weeping, for they will weep at the end. And then their crying can stop, and they will never again weep from this time on.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Overview of the four-fold teaching structure. Introduces the systematic enumeration: three past weepings plus a fourth eschatological one. 'The garments, the sons of the First Man' — cosmological entities identified by their cosmic role. The entire paragraph sets up the degree structure. Impersonal, systematic voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the first time of their weeping is when they had seen the darkness, the enemy being about to burst out against them. They understood everything that would happen to them. They were aware of the one that would rise and come upon them, but by necessity they hastened to him and fought with him. They mastered him, they detained him. They bound him with their body and their limbs, they overcame his death and his fire and his darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Describes the cosmic event: the elements' first encounter with Darkness. 'They bound him with their body and their limbs' — soul-body binding formula applied to the cosmic combat. Both sides internal: light elements vs. Darkness. 'his death and his fire and his darkness' maps qualities of the enemy realm. Process-oriented voice describing what happened within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second time that they wept is [when the]ir father, the First Man, [ascend]ed from the [abyss] of darkness and left them behind; that is the time when he stripped [them off] and left them below. Indeed, when th[ey] s[aw] how the First Man had risen out of the abyss and [l]eft them behind, and that they were abandoned in the enmit[y, th]ey wept and were sore of heart. Still, what could they do, wishing [ ... / ... ] their heart to every affliction. They [remained b]ehind and grew [s]ick under the pressure of the weighty burden of all the works, until the end time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Cosmic geography: the First Man ascending from the abyss, the elements remaining below in mixture. 'the weighty burden of all the works' describes the cosmic condition of entrapment. Lacunae present from manuscript damage. All entities and events are cosmic-internal.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] third time that they wept is when the Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign to lift their heads and rise to the heights from that place; and to pass and journey through all the earths until they should reach the land of tranquilli[t]y and peace, the place of rest prepared for them. So, when they had seen him, that he had separated himself from them, while they themselves remained behind after him and had not ascended; at that moment when they stayed behind these three garments wept. After their crying, they turned their [hear]t to all the heights that were concealed from them, and were of one mind. For [they would] soar up and come to the heights; and pass over all things until the time that was ordained for them all [ ... ] at the end of the worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. The Living Spirit, the three garments of activity (wind, water, fire per ch. 30) — cosmic entities acting within the cosmic system. 'all the earths' and 'the land of tranquillity and peace' are cosmic geography. The entire passage describes the process of ascent through cosmic levels — a systematic emanation/return teaching. 'the time that was ordained for them' — cosmic teleology. The longest substrate paragraph reflects the complexity of this stage.

paragraphs.core_text: [The f]ourth time when they will weep is when the [S]tatue will be taken up on the last day, and they will weep [for] the souls of the liars and blasphemers; for they may give [ ... ] because their limbs have been severed [ ... ] of the darkness. And also [th]ose souls, when the Statue will go up and th]ey are left alo[n]e, they will weep in that they will rema[in] behind in affliction for ever. For they wi[ll be cut off] and separated from the Last Statue. An[d it is] a necessity to take these souls who are ready for loss as retribution for the deeds that they have done. They go i[n to] this [darkne]ss and are bound with the Darkness; just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it. At that very moment, when the Last Statue rises up, the[y wi]ll weep. And then they will scream out loud because they will be severed from the company of this great Statue. And they remain behind for ever. This great weeping [ ... ] is terrible, it occurs in front of the souls and [ ... ] who are ready for loss in accordance with their deeds. And they [will] weep with that crying, they will never be silent; because they will not attain rest from this time on.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration unit — eschatological. The Last Statue is a cosmic entity; souls 'bound with Darkness' uses the binding formula. 'liars and blasphemers' and 'in accordance with their deeds' are moral categories but function as cosmological designations for souls that chose Darkness — the cosmic mechanism of attachment ('they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it'). Both sides remain within the cosmic system: the Statue ascends, lost souls are bound into Darkness. No contemporary institutions or practices are identified. The 'treasure' language describes cosmic attachment, not contemporary behavior.

paragraphs.core_text: So, they too are the garments of these elements. This fourth time of weeping is heart-rending for them. It is much worse for them than these other three times of weeping before. This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep and are heartsore for these soul[s] who will be cut off from peace, because rest will not come about for them, to allow them to rest from torment for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explanatory conclusion to the four-fold cycle. Explains why the fourth is worst — the elements weep not for themselves but for the permanently lost. This closes the teaching structure: overview (P2), first (P3), second (P4), third (P5), fourth (P6), explanation of the fourth (P7). The teaching cycle is complete and self-contained at this point. 'cut off from peace' and 'rest from torment' are cosmic-eschatological conditions, not contemporary applications.

Clear editorial seam. 'Therefore, due to' — bridge connective flagged by NLP pipeline. The teaching about the fourth weeping (cosmic drama) is now APPLIED to justify apostolic mission: 'all the apostles and the fathers, the revealers of the good and the true prophets.' These are institutional/historical categories — one side of the mapping has left the cosmic system and entered the editors' world of apostolic succession. 'the second death' retains cosmic vocabulary but serves the editorial argument. 'Not a single one of all the apostles wished to receive his reward on earth' — hagiographic characterization of apostolic behavior. 'being crucified in their body' echoes Christological/apostolic narrative. This paragraph would be removed without loss to the cosmic teaching, which closed at P7.

Closing admonition addressed to the audience. 'the wise person must constantly be attentive to this lesson' — direct injunction to behavior. 'the gods and the apostles' mixes cosmic ('gods') with institutional ('apostles'). Fragmentary (lacuna at start). Classic devotional closure appended after editorial bridge. Position at chapter end is typical for exhortation layer.
